name: The neutrino oscillation story
notes: Working title. Homestake: the Atlas dates continuous operation from 1970 (a Wikipedia-sourced interval, approximate); the Davis Nobel lecture says the experiment became operational in 1967. The text avoids the start year except the 1998 paper's "since 1970".

steps.text: Homestake, a 100,000-gallon chlorine-argon neutrino detector in a gold mine in Lead, South Dakota, measured the flux of solar neutrinos from 1970. The Sun produces one-third as many neutrinos as expected, wrote Raymond Davis, and this was the solar neutrino problem.
steps.title: The Sun's missing neutrinos

it began operation on 1 April 1996
In June 1998 it found that fewer neutrinos arrived from the opposite side of the Earth than expected, providing compelling evidence for neutrino oscillations

steps.text: Super-Kamiokande is a 50,000-tonne water Cherenkov detector 1000 metres underground in the Kamioka Mine in Japan, and it began operation on 1 April 1996. In June 1998 it found that fewer neutrinos arrived from the opposite side of the Earth than expected, providing compelling evidence for neutrino oscillations.
steps.title: Evidence for oscillations

steps.text: SNO held 1000 tonnes of heavy water, with the centre of its detector vessel 2039 m below the surface in a mine near Sudbury, Canada. In April 2002 it released direct evidence that solar electron neutrinos change flavor, with the non-electron-flavour part of the solar flux 5.3 standard deviations above zero.
steps.title: Heavy water and the solar puzzle

steps.text: KamLAND watched antineutrinos emitted by distant power reactors, typically 180 km away. Its first results, released on 6 December 2002, showed a deficit of events inconsistent with standard antineutrino propagation at the 99.95% confidence level.
steps.title: A deficit of reactor antineutrinos

question.prompt: T2K's neutrinos travel 295 km from J-PARC to Super-Kamiokande. Estimate the travel time, assuming they move at the speed of light.

steps.text: T2K uses an intense proton beam from the J-PARC accelerator in Tokai, Japan, to make a muon neutrino beam aimed 295 km away at Super-Kamiokande. In November 2013 it reported observing electron neutrino appearance in that beam, with 28 electron neutrino events and a significance of 7.3σ.
steps.title: A beam across Japan

claims.covers: NOvA's 14 kt far detector is near Ash River, Minnesota, about 810 km from the neutrino source
Both of its detectors are 14.6 mrad off the beam axis and receive a narrow-band neutrino flux peaked at 1.8 GeV

question.answer: T2K's beam has its peak energy at about 0.6 GeV, which maximizes the effect of the neutrino oscillation at 295 km. For T2K, 295 km ÷ 0.6 GeV ≈ 490 km/GeV, and for NOvA, 810 km ÷ 1.8 GeV = 450 km/GeV. The two ratios differ by only about 9% (490 ÷ 450 ≈ 1.1), although NOvA's baseline is about 2.7 times longer (810 ÷ 295 ≈ 2.7).

question.prompt: T2K's baseline is 295 km and its beam energy peaks at about 0.6 GeV; NOvA's baseline is about 810 km and its beam energy peaks at 1.8 GeV. Compare the ratio of baseline to energy for the two experiments.

steps.text: NOvA's 14 kt far detector is near Ash River, Minnesota, about 810 km from the neutrino source. Both of its detectors are 14.6 mrad off the beam axis and receive a narrow-band neutrino flux peaked at 1.8 GeV.
steps.title: A longer baseline

steps.text: JUNO is a 20 kt liquid-scintillator detector 52.5 km from multiple reactor cores, and it began physics data taking on 26 August 2025. With its first data it measured sin²θ12 = 0.3092 ± 0.0087 and Δm²21 = (7.50 ± 0.12) × 10⁻⁵ eV² for the normal mass ordering scenario, improving the precision by a factor of 1.6 relative to the combination of all previous measurements.
steps.title: A reactor detector in China

summary: Seven stops on the path from the Sun's missing neutrinos to neutrino oscillations measured with beams and reactors.
